title: Ceres Diagnostics - Renewal & Staggered Burst Clauses / VPC Pathway
meeting_header: Date: 2026-10-15; Time: 15:00-15:48 UTC; Duration: 48 minutes; Location: Zoom; Redwood: Samir/Lena/Maya; Ceres: Elena/Tom/Priya
summary: Monthly renewal/expansion check-in focused on contract window options, introducing a staggered burst clause for seasonal load, and clarifying VPC onboarding and KMS expectations. Customer requested a mix of reserved capacity plus a predictable burst buffer and a compliance checklist for SOC2/KMS integration. Redwood to provide redline options and an estimated cost delta for burst tiers plus VPC onboarding runbook.
action_items: Samir - Send 2 redlined contract options (12mo vs 24mo) and three burst-tier addenda - due 2026-10-20
Lena - Share VPC onboarding checklist + estimated provisioning timeline (staging to prod) - due 2026-10-18
Maya - Provide historical usage export (last 90 days) and sample prompts for perf eval - due 2026-10-19
Tom - Confirm internal approval window for 24mo commit and procurement constraints - due 2026-10-22
Priya - Share KMS vendor and any additional encryption requirements for review - due 2026-10-20
next_steps: Redwood to send redlines and burst pricing by Wed (10/20)
Customer to deliver usage data and KMS details for security review
Schedule technical pilot run for EU VPC staging week of 10/25
Follow-up call to review pricing and legal terms on 10/26
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samir from Redwood here, joining with Lena and Maya. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Elena: Hi, Elena Ruiz from Ceres.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Bowers, platform.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, security lead.
[00:15] Samir: Awesome. Goal today is to land on renewal cadence and talk through the burst clause idea you asked about plus VPC pathing. Roughly 45 minutes. Sound good?
[00:25] Dr. Elena: Yep, that's right. We're mainly trying to understand the cost delta for predictable bursts vs increasing base commit. Also need to confirm the KMS flow for private keys.
[00:34] Lena: Quick save, when you say predictable bursts, do you mean scheduled seasonal uplift or on-demand overflow?
[00:40] Dr. Elena: Both, actually. We have scheduled upticks for end-of-quarter processing and occasional ad-hoc spikes when partner plugins run reports.
[00:50] Tom: Our ops ask is we want a cap so we can forecast egress and cost, not surprise bills.
[00:55] Samir: Totally. So we've been experimenting with a staggered-burst addendum — it's basically a committed baseline plus a tiered burst pool with fixed rates per tier and an overage safety cap. Gives predictability.
[01:06] Priya: Important for us is how bursts are routed. If it goes through multi-tenant hosted, we need assurance on data residency and logs. SOC2 is a must.
[01:16] Maya: We'll make sure the burst instances honor the same data controls — audit logs, token redaction, retention policies.
[01:23] [00:30] Lena: Technical note: The burst instances can be spun from your dedicated pool or fall back to a lower-latency hosted variant; there's a kernel-selection path there, but for VPC usage we prefer dedicated farm in your VPC to maintain network egress boundaries.
[00:38] Tom: So the question — do we assign burst capacity to their VPC or do we let Redwood broker it?
[00:43] Samir: You can do either. If you own the dedicated capacity in your VPC (private deployment), you get full control and egress predictability. If you use Redwood-hosted burst, it's faster to activate but less isolated. There's a middle ground — dedicated reserved plus a Redwood-managed burst pool that routes via a private peering link.
[00:58] Priya: We need the private peering approach to pass our security review. It keeps a single egress path from our VPC.
[01:04] Dr. Elena: Risk question — what's the failover if our dedicated pool saturates? We can't have requests hang.
[01:10] Lena: We have automatic fallback policies: canary to a compatible quantized model or route to regionally adjacent cluster. You can configure SLOs — like maintain p95 under 400ms — or prefer cost minimal.
[01:22] Tom: Hmm, p95 400ms might be optimistic during peaks. What's realistic with the current model mix?
[01:27] Lena: For your workload (short prompts, 1-2k tokens typical) in dedicated 8x A100 class, p95 is around 180-220ms. With burst routing to a managed pool you'd see p95 in the 300-500ms window depending on batch width. These are ballpark numbers; we'll run a pilot.
[01:43] [01:30] Samir: On contract structure, two practical options: 12-month renewal with increased baseline + optional burst addendum, or 24-month commit with lower unit price and burst pool included at a discounted rate.
[01:49] Dr. Elena: Procurement would prefer 24mo if the burst pricing is predictable. But our legal needs a staggered clause so we can increase capacity mid-term without a full amendment.
[01:58] Maya: We can draft a staggered-capacity amendment that lists tranches — e.g., +20% at Q2, +50% at Q4 — with pre-defined pricing bands. That avoids renegotiating.
[02:07] Priya: For SOC2 and KMS — we need your KMS integration doc. Primary questions: key rotation policy, who controls keys (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed), and HSM attestation.
[02:19] Lena: Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS (we integrate via VPC endpoints) and Redwood-managed KMS. For Ceres, if you choose CMK (customer-managed keys), we never persist plaintext; we do envelope encryption and only store ciphertext. We can send the KMS architecture doc.
[02:35] Tom: About audit logs — we need token-level tracing and per-request headers logged for three months. Any egress costs for logs?
[02:43] Maya: Audit logs are provided; retention beyond the default window is an add-on. No additional egress for logs within the VPC peering, but long-term storage may incur costs. We'll itemize that.
[02:55] [02:50] Dr. Elena: Timeline wise — we want VPC staging in EU (frankfurt) by end of October, a short pilot the following week, and production by mid-November if approvals land. Is that feasible?
[03:05] Lena: It's tight but doable: provisioning VPC peering, key exchange, and baseline reserved capacity takes 2-3 weeks if procurement and security are responsive. If you can confirm baseline numbers this week, we can aim for staging 10/25.
[03:16] Tom: I'll try to lock down baseline numbers by Friday.
[03:19] Priya: One more on encryption — do you offer bring-your-own-HSM (BYOHSM) options? We need FIPS 140-2 attestations for some workloads.
[03:26] Lena: We don't host customer HSMs inside Redwood; on private deployments you can integrate your HSM via standard KMS bridges. We have customers with HSMs in their VPC that we've integrated. We'll include the integration pattern.
[03:36] [03:30] Samir: Pricing — ballpark numbers: 24mo commit roughly 18% lower unit cost vs 12mo, and burst tiers are priced as fixed increments: Tier A (burst cushion 20% usage) +8%; Tier B (50%) +17%; emergency overage cap kicks in at +40% marginal rate. We'll send a spreadsheet.
[03:53] Dr. Elena: Those increments look reasonable, but procurement needs the exact math. Also want a cancellation clause if we onboard a new partner and shift traffic.
[04:03] Maya: We can offer a limited break clause with 60-day notice tied to a migration event, subject to minimums. We'll flag it in the redlines.
[04:11] [04:00] Tom: On benchmarking — we want Redwood to run three target prompts (we'll share) against the staging cluster to validate p95 and cost per token. Can you run with our sample dataset?
[04:21] Lena: Yes, if you provide the prompts and a small representative dataset, we can run controlled runs and give a profiling report — latency, token cost, batching behavior, and KV cache hit rates.
[04:33] Priya: For the run, can we require that logs exclude PHI? Our prompts sometimes contain redacted patient IDs. Need clarity on redaction.
[04:40] Maya: We'll respect redaction flags; advise to pre-redact any PHI before handing prompts. We'll include guidance.
[04:48] [04:45] Samir: Okay, let's recap actions — I'll produce the two contract options and burst addenda sheet; Lena will send the VPC/KMS runbook and provisioning timeline; Maya will ask for the usage export format and retention options. Ceres to produce usage and KMS vendor details and confirm internal timeline.
[05:03] Dr. Elena: Sounds good. One last off-hand — any updates on regional model variants? We sometimes see different latency in eu-west vs eu-central.
[05:12] Lena: We maintain comparable model variants; differences are mostly infra locality and kernel tuning. We'll include region-specific perf notes in the report.
[05:20] [05:15] Priya: Also, please include a sample SOC2 addendum and a list of sub-processors. We need that for our legal pack.
[05:26] Maya: We'll attach the SOC2 report link and full sub-processor list in the follow-up email.
[05:32] Tom: Great. If we can get the cost spreadsheet and redlines by Wed, procurement will take a look and we'll reconvene.
[05:38] Samir: Perfect. Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the 10/26 pricing review.
[05:44] Dr. Elena: Thanks everyone, bye.
[05:46] [End of recording]
